name: Birmingham
meta_description: Discover Birmingham's beer scene: Victorian pubs, cask ale at The Wellington, Digbeth street food, plus bookable tastings and pub walking tours.
intro_md:
Birmingham rewards drinkers who look past the city-centre chains. Its Victorian pub heritage is remarkable: The Bartons Arms in Aston, all tilework and sweeping staircase, has one of the finest interiors in England, while The Wellington on Bennetts Hill keeps a constantly rotating line-up of cask ales that has made it the city's real-ale institution.

Digbeth is where the newer energy lives. Dig Brew Co makes its beer in an old factory there, and Digbeth Dining Club gathers the city's best street food under the railway arches. For eating more widely, the Balti Triangle in Sparkbrook gave its name to a whole style of curry, and the market halls by the Bullring have fed the city for generations.

Don't miss:

- The Bartons Arms, a Victorian masterpiece in Aston
- Cask ale at The Wellington on Bennetts Hill
- Street food under the arches at Digbeth Dining Club
- A balti on Ladypool Road in the Balti Triangle

gyg_tours.title: Birmingham British Beer Private Guided Tasting Tour
gyg_tours.summary: A private guided tasting tour of Birmingham's pubs and brewing heritage, with four to eight beer tastings depending on the option chosen and optional food pairings. The route passes city landmarks including Birmingham Cathedral and the Library of Birmingham.
gyg_tours.description_md: This private guided tasting tour explores Birmingham's brewing culture with a licensed local guide. You visit a selection of handpicked venues around the city centre, sampling a range of ales and craft beers paired with snacks or a meal, while learning about the city's industrial heritage and pub scene. Three duration options are available, ranging from two to four hours with four to eight beers included.
highlights: Private tour with a licensed local guide
Sample 4 to 8 beers depending on option
Popular, regional and craft beer selections
Beers paired with snacks or a full meal
Learn Birmingham's brewing and industrial heritage
gyg_tours.meeting_point: The Grand Hotel Birmingham, 1 Church St, Birmingham B3 2FE, United Kingdom

gyg_tours.title: Birmingham Slogging Gang Evening Walking Tour with Pub Stops
gyg_tours.summary: An evening walking tour through Birmingham's late 19th-century gang history, led by a guide in Peaky Blinders character, with stops at four drinking establishments ranging from real ale pubs to gin palaces. Drinks are at your own expense.
gyg_tours.description_md: This two-hour guided evening walking tour explores Birmingham's criminal past through the story of the city's late 19th-century slogging gangs. Led by a guide dressed as a Peaky Blinder, you walk through the city centre learning about real gangs such as the Peaky Blinders and the Gun Quarter Gang. The route takes in four local pubs, with drinks included along the way for a genuinely local Birmingham experience.
highlights: Guide dressed as a Peaky Blinder
Learn about the Peaky Blinders and Gun Quarter Gang
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Outside the Apple shop (Apple Birmingham); your guide will be dressed as a Peaky Blinder.

gyg_tours.title: Birmingham: Slogging Gangs Guided Walking Tour
gyg_tours.summary: A two-hour guided walk through Birmingham's back streets telling the story of the city's slogging gangs and the real Peaky Blinders, taking in the Gunmakers Quarter and a local pub along the way.
gyg_tours.description_md: Follow in the footsteps of Edward Shelby and his comrades on a guided walking tour through Birmingham's streets, exploring the history of the city's 19th- and 20th-century slogging gangs. Your guide, in character as Edward Shelby, leads you through hidden corners, dark alleyways and significant landmarks while recounting tales of notorious figures made famous by Peaky Blinders, such as Billy Kimber and Alfie Solomon. The walk includes a stop at a historical local pub for refreshments.
highlights: Guided walk through Peaky Blinders history
Refreshments stop at a historical pub
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Across the street from the old fire station; look for a guide dressed as a Peaky Blinders character (52.4857244, -1.8900586).
